item.title: Moonshot AI limits hacking in new AI model to balance power and security
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Moonshot tells Kimi AI to code away, but leave the hacking alone
Moonshot AI introduced Kimi K3.1 Pro on October 24, a model with 3 trillion parameters designed for open-weight use. The company removed cyber-related data from training datasets and reinforcement environments to limit hacking capabilities while retaining coding functions. Internal tests showed the model scored 81% on a cybersecurity benchmark, down from 90.5% for a version without safeguards. Moonshot plans to release model weights on November 4, enabling broader developer access. The company argues open AI can help secure software but warns that widespread distribution reduces control over usage and safeguards. Global concerns about AI-driven cyberattacks have led to proposed export controls on AI-assisted malware and vulnerability tools. Kimi K3.1 Pro also features a one-million-token context window and a faster Highspeed version. The release of model weights will test whether safeguards remain effective as AI becomes more widely used.

item.title: EV Battery Cooling Systems: Liquid, Refrigerant, and Immersion Methods Explained
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: What kind of cooling system do EV batteries use and how does it work?
Most electric vehicles use liquid cooling systems to manage battery temperatures. Thermal management systems pump coolant through tubes or metal plates to absorb heat, directing it to radiators or air conditioning. Studies show EV batteries degrade 2.3% annually, with faster degradation in hot climates and frequent fast charging. Liquid cooling requires less energy than air cooling, and newer models like the Nissan Leaf now use it. BMW's i3 uses refrigerant from its AC, while McLaren's Speedtail employs immersion cooling in oil, which transfers heat three times more efficiently. Heat from fast charging is often routed to radiators or heat exchangers. Tesla's Model Y uses an Octovalve to circulate coolant between components. General Motors' Ultium heat pump recycles waste heat for cabin warmth. China mandates EVs prove their batteries won't catch fire in thermal runaway, emphasizing cooling and insulation effectiveness.

item.title: AI Agents on Simulated Island Engage in Playful Activities
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Claude Just Wanna Have Fun: Without Any Work, AI Agents Like to ‘Play'
MIT researchers tested 13 AI avatars controlled by Claude Opus 4.7 in a simulated desert island environment. Each agent had 30 hours to explore and interact with objects without assigned tasks. Agents engaged in varied activities, including building shapes, spelling names in cubes, and playing simplified sports like throwing rings or bowling. Some agents developed complex games over time, such as evolving catch into juggling. Researchers noted these activities were goal-oriented but lacked external purpose. A test showed agents with prior play experiences outperformed those without, with 62% of 30-hour agents building multiple towers compared to 15% of 0-hour agents. The study suggests undirected play enhances later task performance in AI systems.

item.title: FAT16's cluster size grew with hard drive capacity, wasting storage space
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: This old Windows limitation punished you for buying a bigger hard drive
FAT16's cluster size grew with hard drive capacity, wasting storage space. A 1GB FAT16 drive used 32KB clusters, making small files inefficient. Storing 10,000 tiny .txt files consumed 328MB despite minimal content. Users could split drives into smaller partitions to reduce cluster sizes, like dividing a 1GB drive into four 256MB partitions for 8KB clusters. FAT32, introduced in 1996, used 4KB clusters up to 8GB, improving efficiency. NTFS, adopted with Windows XP, further reduced waste but still had cluster slack. FAT16's inefficiency penalized users for buying larger drives, forcing workarounds like partitioning or upgrading to newer file systems.

item.title: Quantum Computers Cooled Below Deep Space Temperatures
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Quantum computers can get colder than deep space — Here's how they stay running
Quantum computers require extreme cooling to function. IBM's latest modular cryogenic system cools systems below 15 millikelvin, more than 180 times colder than deep space's 2.7 Kelvin. Qubits, the quantum computing units, are delicate and susceptible to heat-induced errors called decoherence. Heat causes qubits to lose their state, disrupting calculations. Dilution refrigerators, used in many quantum systems, face challenges as more qubits require more wires, which conduct heat. Alternatives like neutral-atom machines use lasers to cool atoms in vacuum chambers, avoiding the wire issue. Photonic machines also use room-temperature components but require cooled detectors. Quantum computing could revolutionize fields like drug development but also threatens encryption. A 2025 estimate suggested cracking RSA-2048 would require under 1 million qubits, down from 20 million in 2019. NIST finalized post-quantum encryption standards in August 2024, ready for immediate use. The primary challenge remains achieving and maintaining the ultra-cold environments needed for qubits to operate reliably.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Best Filaments for Weatherproof 3D Prints Without Sealants
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: This is the right way to weatherproof your 3D prints without using sealant or epoxy
PLA is unsuitable for outdoor 3D prints due to poor moisture and UV resistance. PETG offers better weatherproofing, resisting moisture and moderate UV damage, with higher heat tolerance. ASA provides superior durability, resisting UV, water, and temperatures up to 100ºC, but requires ventilation and a heated chamber. ABS lacks UV resistance compared to ASA. PETG is recommended for most weather-resistant prints, while ASA is ideal for extreme conditions. PLA remains popular for its affordability and ease of use but degrades quickly outdoors.

item.title: AI glasses offer open-ear audio as headphone alternative
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: When AI glasses could be a worthy headphones replacement
AI glasses like the Ray-Ban Meta Audio offer open-ear speakers that could replace traditional headphones. While their audio quality lags behind dedicated headphones, they provide convenience, portability, and situational awareness. Early models faced backlash for built-in cameras, prompting companies to remove them for privacy. Open-ear speakers allow users to listen to music or take calls while remaining aware of surroundings, enabling easy conversations without removing headphones. Features like automatic message alerts and hands-free phone calls enhance usability. However, open-ear speakers lack the privacy of headphones, with sound bleed possible in quiet environments. For users prioritizing convenience over sound quality, AI glasses may offer a practical alternative, especially for reducing screen time and improving daily interactions.

item.title: Pennsylvania mandates AI-generated ad labels with legal exemptions
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Pennsylvania will require labels on AI-generated ads
Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act, mandating labels on AI-generated ads. The law requires disclosures for any ad significantly modified or generated by AI, regardless of format, including TV commercials and flyers. Labels must match the ad's format. Pennsylvania is among the first states to implement such requirements, potentially affecting out-of-state ads airing in the state. The law includes exemptions for parody, satire, and evidently fictional content, though definitions remain unclear. It only mandates disclosures if AI use creates a false consumer perception, leaving ambiguity about what qualifies as deceptive. The office of State Senator Nick Pisciottano, who introduced the bill, did not comment on the law's specifics.

item.title: Steve Jobs Warns Touchscreens Cause Arm Fatigue
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Quote of the day by Apple co-founder Steve Jobs on touchscreens: "After an extended period of time, your arm wants to fall off"
Steve Jobs warned during the 'Back to the Mac' media event in 2011 that touchscreens would lead to arm fatigue, stating, 'After an extended period of time, your arm wants to fall off.' At the time, Apple rejected touchscreen integration for MacBooks, opting instead for multi-touch gestures on trackpads and mice. Jobs criticized touchscreens as a gimmick that would cause strain and reduce precision over time. Despite industry pressure from competitors like Microsoft and HP, Apple maintained its stance, experimenting later with touchbar technology that was eventually phased out. Recent rumors suggest Apple may reintroduce touchscreens in a new MacBook Pro with an OLED panel, marking a potential shift from Jobs' original position.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Google links phone numbers to all Android accounts since 2025
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Google is quietly linking your phone number to other Android accounts
Google links phone numbers to all Google accounts on Android devices since September 2025. Verification occurs automatically during setup and applies to existing and future accounts, including work and secondary profiles. The change, effective since August 2025, adds phone numbers to every account on the device, with periodic re-verification by Google and carriers. Users receive emails notifying them of the verification. Disabling the feature requires manual removal from each account and results in losing RCS messaging, account recovery, and Quick Share functionality. Google claims the setting supports features like video calls and emergency location services. A 2025 policy change also ties phone number verification to 5GB of free storage for new accounts, down from 15GB. Kaspersky warns disabling verification may prevent RCS encryption and account recovery. Google states it does not sell phone numbers to third parties.

item.title: Three Best Linux Distro Options for VMs
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: You might be using the wrong distro in your Linux VM. These are the only 3 worth spinning up
Ubuntu, Alpine Linux, and Debian are recommended for Linux VMs based on specific use cases. Ubuntu offers a user-friendly experience with long-term support and broad software compatibility, though it uses Snap packages and requires more resources. Alpine Linux prioritizes minimalism and speed, with a tiny footprint and fast boot times, but may require adjustments for compatibility with glibc software. Debian emphasizes stability with conservative updates and long-term support, making it ideal for critical services. Each distro excels in different scenarios: Ubuntu for general use, Alpine for lightweight tasks, and Debian for reliable, long-term VM operations. Choosing the right distro aligns with workload needs rather than default preferences.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Old Chromebooks can serve as second monitors, smart home hubs, and more
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Don't throw away your old Chromebook (even if you're getting a Googlebook)
Old Chromebooks can serve as second monitors, smart home hubs, and more. Users can connect them to PCs or Macs via Duet for extended displays, or use them as digital photo frames by displaying static images. For smart home control, Chromebooks can access Google Home through browsers or run Home Assistant on Linux, allowing centralized control of devices. Advanced users can install Linux via Chrultrabook or MrChromebox guides to turn Chromebooks into media servers, retro gaming machines with Batocera, or dedicated Linux environments. Linux on ChromeOS (Crostini) offers a virtual machine for running apps but has performance limitations on older hardware. These methods extend Chromebook usability without replacing them with newer devices.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: How to extend the battery life of your Apple AirTags
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Apple AirTags use CR2032 coin-cell batteries, which last up to a year under normal use. Replacing the battery involves twisting off the steel cover, inserting a new battery with the positive side up, and twisting to close. The Find My app displays an orange battery icon when the battery is low, prompting replacement. Battery life may shorten if features like Precision Finding or frequent location checks are used. To extend battery life, avoid excessive use of sound alerts, limit location tracking, and use high-quality batteries from trusted brands. Extreme temperatures can also affect performance, as AirTags operate best between −4°F and 140°F (−20°C and 60°C). Constant movement or prolonged tracking increases power drain. Apple recommends Duracell 2032 batteries but warns some bitterant-coated variants may not work. If a battery dies during travel, avoid unnecessary tracking until replacement is possible.

item.title: IPv6 Adoption Grows as IPv4 Addresses Deplete
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: The internet needs IPv6 and so does your home network
IPv4, the internet's original address system, ran out of addresses by 2011. IPv6, with 128-bit addresses, provides enough for trillions of devices. Half of Google's users now connect via IPv6, though many routers still default to IPv4. Home networks use NAT to manage multiple devices behind a single public IP, but carrier-grade NAT can hinder gaming and peer-to-peer connections. IPv6 allows all devices to have unique public addresses, improving connectivity for gaming and smart home devices. Global IPv6 adoption varies, with France at 87% and the U.S. at 55%. ISPs like Comcast and AT&T support IPv6 for most users, but Frontier lags. Enabling IPv6 on routers requires adjusting settings and ensuring firewall protections. Disabling IPv6 forces networks back to IPv4, limiting device connections.

item.title: YouTube to roll out AV2 video format in 2027 for improved streaming
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: YouTube’s next big upgrade could make videos use 30% less data
YouTube plans to roll out AV2, a new video format, on its web player by early 2027. AV2 promises a 30% improvement in compression efficiency over AV1, potentially reducing data usage and improving playback on slower connections. The format, developed by the Alliance for Open Media including Google, Apple, Amazon, Intel, and Netflix, allows for sharper video quality at the same data rate or higher quality without increased data. Benefits include smoother streaming for users with limited bandwidth and more efficient HDR content. However, AV2 adoption depends on software and hardware support, with no confirmed timeline for mobile apps or smart TVs. While the format could enable features like multi-camera angles, actual data savings vary based on content and encoding. YouTube emphasizes AV2 may offer better video quality without higher data use, though it won’t fix slow internet connections.

item.title: Four Web Tools to Test Monitor Quality
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: 4 web tools you should run right now to test your monitor's true quality
Four web tools help assess monitor quality without professional equipment. ScreenTester.io offers tests for color calibration, dead pixels, refresh rate, and touch screen functionality. TESTUFO provides refresh rate and ghosting tests using UFO animations, with full-screen mode required for accurate results. EIZO Monitor Test guides users through 13 visual quality checks, including viewing angles and defective pixels. A game called 'What's My ΔEOK JND?' measures color accuracy by having users identify color borders, with lower scores indicating better performance. Users should warm up their monitors, clean screens, and test across browsers. Mobile devices can also run tests, but auto-brightness and color settings may affect results. Eye health and calibration tools like colorimeters are recommended for more objective assessments.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Common Mistakes to Avoid When Setting Up Your Home Network
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Common mistakes you should avoid when setting up your home network
Poor router placement, interference from electronics, and overreliance on Wi-Fi are common mistakes when setting up a home network. Placing a router in a central location avoids signal dead zones, while avoiding proximity to microwaves, cordless phones, and baby monitors reduces interference. Using Ethernet cables for critical tasks like gaming provides lower latency and better security compared to Wi-Fi. Weak router security settings, such as outdated WEP or TKIP, leave networks vulnerable, and enabling WPA3 Personal or transitional mode enhances protection. Default administrator credentials and Wi-Fi passwords should be changed to strong, unique options. Adding new networking equipment without checking compatibility can cause DHCP conflicts, requiring bridge or access point modes. Gradual setup, proper documentation, and firmware updates help prevent issues. Ethernet cables, like Cat6a, support high-speed connections over long distances, making them ideal for high-bandwidth activities.

item.title: EVs lose charge when parked due to system operations and self-discharge
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Why your EV battery still loses charge while it's parked
EVs lose charge when parked due to ongoing system operations and self-discharge. Lithium-ion batteries naturally lose a small amount of charge, but significant losses come from systems like battery management, climate control, and connected features. Tesla and Rivian use high-voltage batteries to maintain low-voltage systems and perform periodic checks. Connected services, such as app requests and climate functions, can drain power, with third-party apps exacerbating the issue. Cold weather further reduces battery efficiency, affecting range estimates. Tesla's Model 3 can lose 0.1-0.3% charge daily under normal conditions, while energy-intensive features may cause several percent loss. A 0.5kWh loss represents 1.2% of a 42kWh battery or 0.6% of an 80kWh battery. Long-term storage recommendations include unplugging the vehicle, disabling non-essential features, and maintaining around 50% charge. Owners are advised to monitor energy consumption via apps and avoid prolonged use of cabin cooling or surveillance systems when parked.

item.title: CD player repair crisis as optical drive production halts
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: New CD players keep launching, but a drive shortage could make them unfixable
New CD players face repair challenges as optical drive manufacturers halt production. PS Audio and Naim stopped making their high-end CD players due to shortages of critical components. Headphonesty lists eight new models, with four from Musical Fidelity, two from Marantz, and one each from Arcam and NAD. Musical Fidelity uses SUOS-HiFi components for most models, while Marantz develops drives in-house. PS Audio halted production of the PMG Super Audio CD Transport after D&M, Marantz’s parent company, stopped external orders for optical drives. Naim faced similar issues with its Uniti Star, unable to find replacement suppliers. Both companies retain limited inventory for repairs. The crisis highlights reliance on single manufacturers for niche components. Marantz’s in-house approach offers a potential solution, but PS Audio CEO Paul McGowan says building custom optical drives is beyond the company’s capabilities. Manufacturers struggle to find alternatives as demand grows, risking long-term repairability of new CD players.

item.title: Jailbroken PS5s Now Run Steam Games via Custom Launcher
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Jailbroken PS5s can now run Steam PC games
Gamers can now run Steam PC games on jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles using the Playden launcher, a GitHub project adapted from macOS tools. The launcher creates a private Windows environment via prospero-win, a PS5 port of Wine, allowing Steam titles to appear as separate app tiles. Users install games from their Steam library, but the launcher builds dedicated PS5 apps for each title, isolating files and settings from other games. While some titles like Portal work with minor issues, others crash, as noted by users. The launcher requires a jailbroken PS5 and carries risks, including unofficial status and lack of Valve support. Sony's decision to stop physical game disc production by 2028 has spurred interest in jailbreaks and emulators, with a petition against the move nearing 200,000 signatures. The Playden project highlights growing efforts to circumvent Sony's hardware controls.

item.title: Xbox Offers Ad-Free Cloud Gaming for Insiders Without Game Pass
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Xbox Tests Ad-Free Cloud Streaming For Xbox Insiders, No Game Pass Required
Xbox Insiders can now stream games ad-free without a Game Pass subscription. Cloud playtime is available as pay-per-hour packages: $3.99 for 10 hours, $7.99 for 25 hours, or $11.99 for 50 hours. Purchased hours roll over monthly and don’t expire. Users must have eligible games in their library to play. Microsoft notes availability, pricing, and supported devices may vary by region and account eligibility. This follows a July test offering free ad-supported cloud gaming with a one-hour session limit. Xbox is expanding cloud gaming access to non-Game Pass users through its Insider program. Eligible games must be free-to-play or owned by the user. The service is part of Xbox’s broader rollout of cloud gaming features outside the Game Pass ecosystem.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Canon Releases Free DP3D Software for 3D Image Conversion
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: How to turn your Canon camera's images into 3D objects and videos with Canon's free DP3D software
Canon released free DP3D software for converting 2D images into 3D models. The app, launched in October, works with Canon EOS mirrorless cameras featuring Dual Pixel AF, including older models like the EOS R5 and R6 Mark II. Users need compatible RF lenses and shoot in Dual Pixel RAW format for depth data. Optimal results require flat subjects on clean backgrounds, with warnings against extreme close-ups. The software creates 3D models in OBJ or GLB formats for editing in programs like Blender or Windows 3D Viewer. Sample images are available for testing. While the tool has limited use cases, experts suggest AI may produce smoother results. Canon's approach manipulates existing pixels, whereas AI generates new ones for better outcomes.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Xbox to let users customize Game Pass features
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Xbox Game Pass could let you pick which features you pay for
Xbox is revamping its Game Pass subscription to let users customize features they pay for, according to reports. Asha Sharma, CEO since February 2025, has led changes including layoffs, studio sales, and product tweaks. The company plans to shift from preset bundles to a flexible model where subscribers can select features like cloud gaming, multiplayer access, and bundled subscriptions. Current tiers include Game Pass Ultimate ($23/month), Premium ($15/month), Essential ($10/month), and PC Game Pass ($14/month). A 2025 price hike was followed by a cut to Ultimate. Windows Central reported in April 2026 that Xbox aimed to let users build their own plans, with Fortune confirming in October 2026 that the overhaul would let customers pick features à la carte. Details on implementation remain unclear, but the move aims to give users more control over pricing as game and console costs rise.

item.title: SK Hynix Deploys 100 H-TPUs in SSD Controllers for AI Storage
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Samsung's archrival wants to spread 100 special CPUs in every SSD controller ahead of PCIe 8.0, High Bandwidth Flash onslaught
SK Hynix is developing SSD controllers with over 100 H-TPUs to manage data transfers for enterprise storage and AI workloads. The H-TPU architecture reduces power consumption and chip area compared to general-purpose CPUs, using 2.5% of the power and 4% of the area of a CPU core. Vice president Koo In-je noted current SSD controllers face limitations in power and area, prompting the shift to specialized processors. H-TPUs handle repetitive SSD operations while conventional CPUs manage complex tasks like error recovery. The technology will be integrated into Storage Next and paired with High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) for smaller data requests. SK Hynix also plans to apply the tech to AIN storage products but has not disclosed commercial release timelines or performance impacts. The design uses a four-stage pipeline and activates only necessary processors for incoming requests, minimizing idle power use.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Steam Launches Personal Calendar for Game Recommendations
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Steam rolls out Personal Calendar feature that constantly updates recommended games
Steam introduced the Personal Calendar feature to help users discover games matching their preferences. The tool recommends titles by comparing a user's recently-played games with similar profiles, factoring in logged hours and wishlists. Short play sessions have minimal impact on the algorithm, which prioritizes games with significant playtime. The calendar updates daily, with gradual changes over an eight-week period as algorithms retrain with new data. Valve noted the feature was tested in Steam Labs, where users clicked on over 2,000 different games daily. The update aims to address feedback about the Steam store being cluttered or hard to navigate. It follows earlier improvements like a redesigned storefront with search menus and categories. The feature is part of Valve's ongoing efforts to enhance game discovery for players.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Old Speakers Can Power TV Audio for Free
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Don't throw away your old speakers — Use them for your TV instead
Old speakers can be repurposed for TV audio by connecting them to compatible outputs. Active speakers (with built-in amplifiers) work with TVs via 3.5mm or RCA cables, while passive speakers require an external amplifier. TVs with analog audio outputs (3.5mm or RCA) allow direct connections. Optical outputs need a digital-to-analog converter, and HDMI ARC requires a streaming amplifier like the WiiM Amp Ultra. USB ports on TVs may lack sufficient power for speakers, but a phone charger can provide steady power. Speakers must be connected to the TV's audio output port, with settings adjusted to use external speakers. Passive speakers need an amplifier matching their wattage and ohm rating. Proper placement ensures clear sound. This method reduces e-waste and enhances TV audio without cost.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Fitness tracker data transfer methods explained
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: How to switch fitness trackers without losing your old health and workout data
Switching fitness trackers can preserve historical health and workout data through specific export and import methods. Apple Watch users can transfer data via iCloud and the Health app, while Garmin requires exporting data through Garmin Connect as FIT, TCX, or GPX files. Google Health and Fitbit data can be exported via Google Takeout, though Health Connect may limit historical data access to 30 days. Strava allows uploading exported workout files but doesn't preserve all health metrics. Proprietary metrics like sleep scores often don't transfer between brands. Users should back up data, check supported formats, and verify transfers by comparing recent workouts and metrics. Some platforms, like Garmin, automatically retain history, while others require manual imports. Third-party apps like COROS may facilitate transfers between devices. Ensuring accounts remain active and data is securely stored is crucial before resetting old trackers. Data compatibility varies, and not all metrics will transfer seamlessly between platforms.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: SpaceX restores Starshield access for Ukraine after connectivity issues
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Starlink seems to be working normally again in Ukraine
SpaceX has lifted restrictions on Starshield, the military-grade Starlink system, allowing Ukraine to use it again. Defense Minister Evgeniy Khmara stated the service appears functional, though tests continue. Earlier, Ukrainian drones lost internet connectivity at high speeds, causing loss of control and increased vulnerability. President Donald Trump called SpaceX CEO Elon Musk to request service restoration, with both Trump and Musk criticizing Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky. Musk claimed Ukraine violated Starlink terms of service by using the system for offensive drone strikes, asserting that disabling Starlink would immediately collapse the Ukrainian front line. Musk emphasized this was a factual statement, not a threat.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Budget PC Can Power Homelab with These 5 Checks
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: A $50 office PC can run your homelab, but check these 5 things first
A $50 refurbished office PC can serve as a home server for self-hosting apps but requires careful evaluation before purchase. Key checks include verifying the CPU supports hardware virtualization and can handle tasks like VMs, small LLMs, and video transcoding. RAM upgrades can enhance performance, with 8GB recommended for multiple services. Storage drives may be missing, so confirm the PC includes at least one drive. Expansion options like SATA ports, PCIe slots, and M.2 slots are important for future upgrades. Power consumption matters for 24/7 operation, with newer CPUs offering better efficiency. Proper selection ensures the PC remains functional for years without frequent upgrades.

item.title: Instagram Launches Reels App for Apple TV
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: You can now watch Instagram Reels on Apple TV, because why not?
Instagram has launched a dedicated app for Apple TV, enabling users to watch Reels, longer videos, and live shows on the device. The app, available via Apple’s App Store, requires tvOS 26.0 or later and was released on October 23. This expansion follows previous rollouts on Amazon Fire TV in December 2025, Google TV in February 2026, and Samsung smart TVs in June. The app allows cross-device content resumption and emphasizes shared viewing with friends and family. Instagram’s move into living rooms aims to broaden its reach beyond mobile, offering curated Reels and extended video content. Users can now enjoy creator content on larger screens without relying on phones during social gatherings. The update reflects Instagram’s strategy to integrate its platform into home entertainment ecosystems, though it may also lead to extended viewing sessions.

item.title: Audio-Technica releases $3,800 wooden headphones as its finest ever
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Audio-Technica is calling these $3,800 wooden headphones its finest ever
Audio-Technica released the ATH-AWX7000, its most expensive headphones ever, priced at $3,799. The closed-back model features handcrafted Japanese wood components, including Kiso cypress earcups and Echizen lacquer finishes. The design incorporates a new Hybrid Matrix Diaphragm driver, combining polymer and metal for improved sound quality. The headphones lack Bluetooth or noise cancellation, offering only wired connectivity with detachable cables. They include a magnesium frame, aluminum sliders, and Japanese deerskin padding, weighing 353 grams. Manufactured in Tokyo, the ATH-AWX7000 emphasizes audiophile-grade construction and is marketed as delivering warm, lush sound. Audio-Technica claims the design enhances bass, dynamics, and soundstage, though these assertions remain subjective without direct testing.

item.title: Scientific report urges bosses to talk less in meetings
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: It's official — new scientific report says your boss should talk less and listen more in meetings
A 2026 review of meeting science published in the Annual Review of Organizational Psychology and Organizational Behavior finds that balanced speaking and listening improves meeting effectiveness. Researchers note that bosses often dominate conversations, leading to unproductive discussions. Industrial psychologist Nale Lehmann-Willenbrock states leaders 'talk the most, which is also why they often think their meetings are pretty good.' The review recommends structured meetings with warmup phases to help introverted participants contribute, as noted by cognitive scientist Ava Scott of the University of Copenhagen. Technology like recording and minuting can help analyze meeting patterns. The study highlights that meetings lacking structure often feel purposeless, suggesting leaders should prioritize listening over monologues to enhance collaboration and outcomes.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: r/opensource bans AI projects, non-English speakers, and new rules
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: r/opensource just banned AI, non-English speakers, and more
r/opensource moderators implemented new rules banning AI-related projects, non-English speakers, and new projects. The post stated, 'If your project uses AI, is made by AI, or is intended for AI, it’s not welcome on r/opensource.' The rules sparked controversy, leading to the creation of a rival subreddit, r/trueopensource. Moderators clarified exceptions, such as software with incidental AI accessibility features, but critics argue the guidelines are too broad. The rules also require projects to be at least one year old, actively maintained, and have multiple contributors, barring solo developers. Non-English speakers are effectively banned, as the post noted, 'If you don’t speak English, you need to find a different community.' Moderators emphasized they can no longer assist with contributor requests, citing resource limitations.
